summary: The note explains the constitutional basis of the office of Governor of Colima, a Mexican state. Under the Political Constitution of the Free and Sovereign State of Colima, executive power is vested in one individual called the Constitutional Governor. The governor serves a six-year term with no reelection, running from November 1 of the election year to October 31 six years later.
one_line: Describes the constitutional role, six-year non-reelectable term, and term dates of the Governor of Colima, Mexico.
key_facts: The Political Constitution of the Free and Sovereign State of Colima places the exercise of the Executive Power of Colima in a single individual.
The individual holding this office is called the Constitutional Governor of the Free and Sovereign State of Colima.
The Constitutional Governor of Colima is chosen for a period of 6 years.
The Constitutional Governor of Colima is not eligible for reelection.
The term of the Governor of Colima begins November 1 of the year of the election.
The term of the Governor of Colima finishes October 31 after six years have elapsed.
Colima is described in the note as a Mexican entity (a free and sovereign state).
